prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Kansas City Missouri for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on your exact needs (single tooth vs. full-arch, bone grafting needed, sedation preference), your insurance/ budget, and what qualities matter most to you (years of experience, lab partnerships, esthetic results, etc.). I can help you find a top provider in Kansas City, MO — but first here’s a practical way to identify the best clinician for your case.

Who to look for
- Specialists who commonly place implants: oral & maxillofacial surgeons, periodontists, and prosthodontists. Many experienced general dentists also place implants, but for complex cases you’ll usually want a specialist.  
- Board certified or fellowship-trained clinicians (e.g., American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics, or fellowship in implant dentistry).

Where to search
- American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) “Find a Dentist”.  
- American Dental Association (ADA) “Find-a-Dentist”.  
- State of Missouri dental board (for license status and disciplinary history).  
- Local reviews (Google, Yelp) and before/after photos on the practice website. Referrals from your general dentist are often very helpful.

Important questions to ask any candidate
- How many implant placements do you perform per year, and how many of this specific type?  
- Are you board-certified or fellowship-trained in implant dentistry?  
- Do you use CBCT (3D) imaging and guided implant planning?  
- Will the same clinician place the implant and restore the crown (or who handles the restoration)?  
- What implant systems do you use and why?  
- What is your success rate and how do you manage complications?  
- Do you provide sedation or anesthesia options?  
- Can I see before/after photos and talk to former patients or read case reviews?  
- What is the full estimated cost (implant, abutment, crown, any grafting) and payment/financing options?

Red flags
- No clear credentials or inability to explain their experience.  
- No CBCT or clear treatment plan for complex cases.  
- Poor reviews describing complications without follow-up care.  
- Upfront pressure to decide or pay before proper imaging/consultation.

Cost ballpark (approximate)
- Single implant (implant + abutment + crown): commonly $2,000–$5,000 or more depending on practice and complexity. Bone grafting or sinus lift adds cost. Full-arch solutions vary widely ($15k–$50k+ depending on approach).

If you want, I can:
- Look up and list highly rated implant specialists in Kansas City, MO (I’ll need a ZIP code or neighborhood if you want proximity).  
- Draft an email or question list you can use when contacting offices.  

Which would you prefer?
